flagged_as_possibly_distinct_blend.summary_review: One of the better-reviewed Lampert cigars; consistent richness, though shows typical Flying Pig burn issues.

critic_reviews.key_notes_text: Praised for richness; uses a different wrapper (Ecuadorian criollo vs. Connecticut on standard Oro vitolas), different bands, and longer-aged filler than the rest of the Oro Line.

flagged_as_possibly_distinct_blend.note: Marketed under the Oro banner but halfwheel confirms it is a genuinely distinct sub-blend (different wrapper, bands, aging), not just another shape of the same blend as Don Patron/El Gringo/Señorito/Gatsby. Flagging separately rather than folding it into the plain vitola list - may warrant its own line entry depending on how Claude Code's loader wants to model 'same blend, different shape' vs 'different blend, same family name'.

research_notes: Photo-library names 'Short-Perfecto' and 'Small-Batch' refer to ONE vitola, officially named 'Small Batch Short Perfecto' - not two separate items. Continental-52 and Platino appear associated with Lampert's separate 'Black Card' exclusive membership program per a retailer listing, but Lampert's own Black Card page gives no blend/vitola specs, so these could not be confirmed as Oro Line catalogue items - excluded rather than guessed. No evidence at all was found for Corona, Culebra, El-Jefe, Emperador, La-Senora, Maduro, or a plain 'Toro-Grande' as Oro Line products via any retailer, review site, or the official site - these could reflect mislabeled photos, unreleased/prototype names, or a different sub-line (Black Card or an Edición series) not yet documented online. RECOMMEND the user double-check these specific photo files before uploading.
